bearings.paper_claim: Few-shot prompting with a codebook of strong and weak agency and communion cues, positive poles only, reaches macro-F1 0.77 (DeepSeek-V3) and 0.76 (GPT-4o) on strong-balanced human labels, the two top configurations. The paper says only these two models pass the functional test units, on strong labels.
bearings.paper_location: Sec 3.2.2 p.8; Sec 4.2 Table 2 p.10; Sec 4.3 Fig 4 p.12
bearings.system_side: agency_communion_llm.py ports the codebook and the positive-pole rule (lines 56-60), weights strong cues 1.0 and weak 0.5 (line 232), and runs an 18-unit self-test (lines 99-121: 3 agency, 3 communion, 6 opposite-pole, 6 unrelated) with a pass bar of 16 of 18 (line 121). Default model is claude-sonnet-5 (line 24).
bearings.transfer_conditions: The paper's macro-F1 figures belong to GPT-4o and DeepSeek-V3 on German sentences scored against three trained coders. The system has no human-labelled sentence test, so its macro-F1 is unknown. The 18 units were written by the builder in English; the paper's Appendix J was not available. Only the design and the functional gate transfer.
bearings.verifier_note: Paper Sec 4.3 p.12: on strong labels only few-shot GPT-4o and DeepSeek-V3 classify all 18 units; on weak plus strong labels only DeepSeek-V3 does. The rel's 'these two models alone pass all 18' overstates. Code matches the paper's design. The code docstring at line 8 calls the comparator fine-tuned RoBERTa; the paper uses XLM-RoBERTa.

bearings.paper_claim: Models told to detect only strong cues perform better than strong-plus-weak definitions, as expected. Table 2 gives DeepSeek-V3 few-shot balanced 0.77 (strong, SD 0.02) against 0.76 (weak plus strong, SD 0.01). No delta is reported.
bearings.system_side: sentences_for keeps every self-referential sentence and weights weak cues 0.5 (lines 124-151, 232). The cache stores the strength label (line 219), but no strong-only score is computed. agency_raw and communion_raw count labels without the weighting, so they are not strong-only scores.
bearings.transfer_conditions: The 0.01 gap sits inside the reported SDs and is a single configuration, so the paper supports a direction, not a magnitude. A strong-only score could be computed from the existing cache at no API cost to test whether member ordering changes.
bearings.verifier_note: The paper's superiority claim is qualitative ('as expected'), and the table gap is 0.01 within SD 0.01-0.02. The rel quotes the numbers correctly, but 'work better' should read as the paper reporting them as better by a margin inside its own SDs. System-side facts confirmed.

bearings.paper_claim: Party-level communion share falls from left to right on CHES: LINKE 19 percent, Greens 12, SPD 10, CDU 8, AfD and FDP about 6. The paper shows regression lines and standard-error bars but gives no coefficients, N or intervals in the main text.
bearings.system_side: The brain note records a party signature of D .099 against R .049 for the Claude instrument, and says the top communion members are progressive Democrats. These figures were not recomputed from data in this check.
bearings.transfer_conditions: Six German parties against a two-party US Congress, with sentence-level shares against member-level scores. The paper gives no pooled coefficient to compare magnitudes. The gap supports convergent validity but also means the persona score carries party, so any pooled use is UNSTRATIFIED across D and R.
bearings.verifier_note: Paper side confirmed at the cited pages, including the party shares and the absence of coefficients. The system-side numbers come from the brain note and were not rechecked against data.

bearings.paper_claim: The construct is the projected public persona under a lens model. The authors state that the relative weight of intrinsic personality and strategic self-presentation in any cue cannot be determined. The paper reports no behavioural outcome linking agency or communion to responsiveness or persuadability.
bearings.system_side: receptivity_layer.py computes persona_susc_z = .60 z(communion) - .40 z(agency) over all members with at least 15 classified sentences, z-scored across parties together (lines 150-155), and blends it at PERSONA_W 0.30 (lines 147, 191). Comments at lines 140-142 cite the cue shares next to the Byrne-style mapping.
bearings.transfer_conditions: The paper supports measuring the projected persona only. The communion-to-susceptibility direction and the .60/.40 weights are design priors (Byrne-style), not findings of this paper. The PERSONA_W keep ruling belongs to the owner and is not revisited here.
bearings.verifier_note: Paper side confirmed: the cannot-be-determined statement is at lines 121-122 (p.3), and the paper has no outcome test. System-side formula, weights and pooling confirmed in code. The brain-sourced H4 result was not rechecked.

bearings.paper_claim: Three coders (the first author and two RAs) reached Krippendorff alpha of .70 to .78 for agency and communion, and .72 to .73 for detecting any cue. The paper calls this acceptable and sufficient in Sec 3.2.1.3 and 4.1 and moderate in Sec 5. No computational model exceeded macro-F1 0.80.
bearings.paper_location: Sec 3.2.1.3 p.8; Sec 4.1 p.9; Table 1 p.10; Sec 5 p.14
bearings.system_side: The 2026-07-04 brain ruling, as cited by the rel, says the paper's coders reached only alpha about .72 on an easier ternary task, and uses that to set aside the single-rater gold test (agency rho +0.035, communion -0.245, n=30). Not recomputed here.
bearings.transfer_conditions: The paper's alpha is a multilabel agreement measure on sentence cue labels, from three trained coders with a codebook. The single-rater test used 1-9 holistic member ratings. The paper does not call its task easier, and .72 is the presence-detection alpha rather than the agency or communion alpha.
bearings.verifier_note: The paper calls alpha above .70 acceptable and agreement sufficient (Sec 3.2.1.3, 4.1), and uses 'moderate' only in the Sec 5 summary. 'Reached only' and 'easier ternary task' are the analyst's framing, not the paper's. The paper's measure is multilabel, not ternary.

bearings.paper_claim: Ramey et al. used a pretrained Mairesse SVR, which the paper says lacks validation against human-annotated data and appears outdated. The paper's own bag-of-words SVM, modelled on Ramey's approach, scores 0.55 to 0.63 macro-F1 on its cue task and often fails to reach 50 percent of functional test units.
bearings.system_side: The big5_traits.py header says the Mairesse SMOreg model file is licence-bound, so the build uses published standardized correlates as linear weights, linear instead of SVR (lines 13-16). The brain says the active weights were later refit to RKH and saved as mairesse_smoreg.json; the mean held-out r of 0.350 is brain-sourced.
bearings.transfer_conditions: The SVM numbers are the authors' own cue-classification results, not member-level trait regression, so they do not measure this component's accuracy. The critique bites harder because RKH, the reference standard, is itself built on Mairesse-type SVR (paper Sec 2.5 p.5 on Ramey et al.).
bearings.verifier_note: The rel says 'on their task' (Ramey's), but the SVM numbers are the authors' own baseline on their cue task, and Ramey's own measures were not tested. The 'Mairesse SMOreg weights' description conflicts with the file header, which describes linear weights from published correlates.

bearings.paper_claim: LLM prompting with a codebook and few-shot examples classifies defined sentence-level cues. Most sentences carry no cue: 94 percent 'none' for strong cues and 89 percent for weak plus strong.
bearings.system_side: big5_llm.py asks 20 IPIP-style observer-keyed items, 4 per trait, at item level with 3-point responses. 'Cannot tell' maps to 0 because cues are absent in about 90 percent of political sentences (header lines 3-10). The header explicitly rejects holistic trait rating. The +0.064 diagonal and the 0.12 bar are brain-sourced; 0.064 was found in the brain, but 0.12 was not located.
bearings.transfer_conditions: The paper validates a narrow codebook cue task, not item-level Big Five ratings, so its success does not transfer to the Pink reader. Treating cannot-tell as 0 matches the paper's base rate, but it is the builder's design choice.
bearings.verifier_note: The paper claim is accurately summarized. The rel calls the Pink reader 'holistic Big Five items', which contradicts big5_llm.py, whose design is explicitly item-level. The 0.12 threshold was not found in the brain text checked.

bearings.paper_claim: On the paper's personality-cue task, few-shot LLM prompting (0.77) beats fine-tuned XLM-RoBERTa (0.70, strong balanced), which only slightly beats a bag-of-words SVM (0.63 strong balanced; 0.55 to 0.63 across variants).
bearings.system_side: train_stance_domain.py --tune builds a word plus char_wb TF-IDF union with a LinearSVC C grid chosen by CV on train only (lines 74-92). The brain reports the production SVM (word plus char, C=2.0) at 83.9 percent accuracy and 0.816 macro-F1 on the untouched n=87 test, and a transformer at 0.757. These brain figures were not rerun.
bearings.transfer_conditions: Different task (CU press and social stance, not German agency and communion cues) and a different baseline: the paper's SVM is word-only with no C tuning. The system's ranking comes from its own held-out test, so this paper cannot rank the system's readers. The code's transformer defaults to distilroberta, not XLM-RoBERTa.
bearings.verifier_note: Paper ordering and numbers confirmed against Table 2 and the Sec 4.2 text. The code contains the tuned word plus char LinearSVC path. The 83.9, 0.816 and 0.757 figures are brain-sourced and were not rerun.

related.why: The paper takes its agency and communion definitions, its positive-pole rule and its 18 functional test items from the PoliPers framework (Sec 3.2.1.1 p.7; Sec 4.3). Item title confirmed.

The paper critiques Ramey et al. on validation (no human labels, outdated SVR). This is a method critique, not a contradiction of Ramey's findings. Note the year mismatch: the paper's reference list gives 2019, PSRM 7(1), but the item says 2016.
Meta-analysis of Big Five and LIWC links, relevant to the closed-vocabulary baseline the paper critiques. The paper does not cite it, so the link is the analyst's, not the paper's.
The paper cites Azucar, Marengo and Settanni 2018 (PAID 124: 150-159) for the claim that automated personality prediction performs comparably to traditional approaches (Sec 2.5 p.5). Item matches.
Not cited by the paper. It is a general guide to LLMs for political text classification, relevant background for the prompting-versus-fine-tuning result.
Not cited by the paper. It is the source of the Byrne-style choking composite in receptivity_layer.py (line 189), where the communion-to-susceptibility mapping originates, not the paper.
Not cited by the paper. Expert trait ratings of US senators are a possible multi-rater criterion for future persona validation, which the paper does not test.

summary_issues: Overall: no bearing is refuted outright. Three are reproduced on the paper side (party gradient, receptivity-layer scope, stance ordering), and five are softened for overstatement or wrong attribution.

Functional test overstated: GPT-4o classifies all 18 units only on strong labels. On weak plus strong labels only DeepSeek-V3 does (paper Sec 4.3 p.12). The summary sentence 'Only GPT-4o and DeepSeek pass the 18-unit functional test' should say so.

Debate figures lack a denominator and window. The 63/37 and 59/41 agency-communion splits are shares of personality-cue sentences for each candidate. Cue shares are about 23 percent (Harris) and 10 percent (Trump) of utterances; n is 655 (Trump) and 320 (Harris). One debate, 10 Sep 2024, machine-translated from English to German with DeepL.
The 45,000 total sentences is implied (15,000 per source, three sources). The paper never states the total; the summary presents it as fact.

Paul attribution unsupported: every paul_markup note in the item is blank and paul_entries has no takeaways. The quoted phrase 'bag-of-words SVM baselines outdated' is the paper's own wording about Ramey (p.5), not a Paul note. The claims about Paul endorsing LLM readers, the gold-panel note and the stance SVM annotation need a source or should be removed.

Corpus description is off: agency_communion_llm.py queries the whole speeches table with a self-reference filter (lines 127-138). It does not restrict to floor and hearing speech. The big5 comment says that table holds CREC, INTERVIEW and legacy CHRG rows.
The Pink reader is called 'holistic' Big Five items. big5_llm.py is item-level by design (20 IPIP-style items, 4 per trait).

The Mairesse SMOreg description conflicts with big5_traits.py, whose header says published standardized correlates were used as linear weights, not the Mairesse model. The brain says the refit weights are saved as mairesse_smoreg.json.

Ramey citation year: the paper's reference list gives Ramey, Klingler and Hollibaugh 2019, PSRM 7(1): 163-184. The item, the code header and the brain all say 2016. The item metadata should be reconciled.

Amsalem link dropped: the paper cites Amsalem et al. 2020, 'Fine-Grained Analysis of Diversity Levels in the News', for media visibility, not the 2018 personality paper in the research vault. The 'cites' relation was therefore unsupported and the item is not in the related list.
Byrne, Ornstein, Mondak and Koutsoumpis are not cited by the paper. The rel wording implies the paper points to them; their links are the analyst's additions and are labelled complements.

Paper-internal rounding: Sec 4.1 p.9 gives 63 percent communion and 38 percent agency for weak plus strong cues, which sum to 101 percent. Flag as a paper-side inconsistency; it does not change any bearing.

Brain-sourced figures were not rechecked against data: party signature D .099 vs R .049; H4 +0.067 against a 0.094 floor; Pink diagonal +0.064 against a 0.12 bar (0.12 not located); mean held-out r 0.350; stance 83.9 percent, 0.816 and 0.757.
Strong-only superiority: the paper reports no delta, and the Table 2 gap is 0.01 within SD (see the qualifies bearing on strong-only).
The code docstring (agency_communion_llm.py lines 7-8) says the paper's comparator is fine-tuned RoBERTa. The paper uses XLM-RoBERTa. This is a code-side wording nit.
